linkedin:
A base64 secret with padding was enough to stop a NIP-46 pairing from ever completing.

Amber 6.6.6 fixes a nostrconnect:// parser that split each query parameter on every = and rejoined the pieces with Kotlin's joinToString, whose default separator is a comma and a space. A secret of XQUdha4rjh_gjAgHN8X5yg== came back as XQUdha4rjh_gjAgHN8X5yg, , in the connect response.

NIP-46 says the client MUST validate the secret returned by the connect response, precisely to avoid connection spoofing. So the client was right to refuse, and the handshake ended there. The spec puts no restriction on the secret alphabet, so padded base64 was always legal.

The fix is a splitParam helper that splits once, on the first = only, plus the same default-separator correction at a second call site and seven new test cases.

We read the diff rather than the changelog. Both agree here, which is not always the case.

Amber 6.6.6 fixes a nostrconnect:// parser that corrupted any connection secret containing =. Splitting each param on every = and rejoining with Kotlin's default ", " separator turned XQUdha4rjh_gjAgHN8X5yg== into XQUdha4rjh_gjAgHN8X5yg, , so the client's mandatory secret check failed and the pairing never completed.

NIP-46 requires that check to avoid connection spoofing, and it sets no restriction on the secret alphabet. The fix splits on the first = only, corrects the same mistake at a second call site, and adds seven tests.
